budget_items.what_was_recorded: Terri B. raised the associated costs of unemployment, noting a figure of 50% of salary plus health insurance costs; Heather had not heard about it.
budget_items.quote: terri b. brought up associated costs of unemployment--50% of salary, health insurance costs?

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Heather L. said the Town qualifies under the CARES Act for reimbursement of up to a stated amount for COVID-19 expenses.
budget_items.quote: heather l. said under the cares act, the town qualifies for a reimbursement of up to $1,028,000 for expenses the town incurs as a result of covid19.

budget_items.topic: FEMA and CARES cost-share for COVID-19 expenditures
budget_items.what_was_recorded: Heather L. said FEMA reimburses 75% of COVID-19 costs and the CARES Act reimburses the remaining 25%.
budget_items.quote: heather l. stated that fema reimburses the town 75% of the cost incurred related to covid 19 and that the cares act will reimburse the town the remaining 25%.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Uncalculated pandemic costs were noted, including employees who do not return to work; Heather said the Town is not obligated to hold positions for those who decline.
budget_items.quote: uncalculated costs with respect to pandemic.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Dave P. asked at what point the Town might set aside its free cash policy to preserve jobs; John H. said using free cash to mitigate longer-term costs seemed a good use.
budget_items.quote: free cash is money available to the town… at what point might we decide to throw that policy out the window

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Terri suggested postponing capital expenditures until Town Meeting in November; Peter said he is less comfortable funding capital projects except in emergencies such as the Flat Hill culvert.
budget_items.quote: terri suggested that given the uncertainty of future revenues and expenses the town should consider postponing capital expenditures until town meeting in november.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Peter cited replacing the Flat Hill culvert as an example of an emergency capital project that could still be funded.
budget_items.quote: except in the case of emergency circumstances--e.g. replacing the flat hill culvert.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Peter stated that roughly one-third of the Town's savings comes from the school department's salary reserve fund, and the teacher's contract expires in about a month.
budget_items.quote: roughly one-third of the town's savings comes from the school department's salary reserve fund.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Terri noted the stabilization account is about $3 million and suggested looking at how comparable towns are handling this.
budget_items.quote: the most conservative approach 105 stabilization account is about $3 million.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Peter B. observed that debt retirement between 2020 and 2024 is relatively small; Dave P. asked what a credit rating decline would cost in increased debt costs.
budget_items.quote: peter b's observation is how relatively small the retirement of debt between 2020 and 2024 is.

budget_items.what_was_recorded: Dave P. hopes the Town can purchase the streetlights, since LED streetlights would reduce operating costs.
budget_items.quote: dave p. strongly hopes that the town can find its way to purchase the streetlights.
